text: anya: Quick flag from today's bring-up: rnrk-v4-int8 shows neutral NDCG but top-1 MRR drops ~3.7% concentrated on docs with HTML fragments and long query-string URLs. cole: Any short repro from holdout? anya: Example pair: ``` query: \"download map tile with api key\" fp16_doc: \"Use the tiles endpoint: link Make sure to include & in params.\" -> rank 1 ptq_doc: \"To fetch tile hit https://maps.example.com/tiles/12/123/456?key=ABC&mode=png Note: watch html-escapes & and params.\" -> drops to rank 4 on int8 ``` marta: Hmm. HTML escapes (&, <) and concatenated query params often produce punctuation-heavy tokenization. Did we verify tokenizer parity during packaging? anya: I ran a tokenizer diff: fp16 keeps ['&', 'amp', ';'] separate, ptq artifact merges into one token ' &'. Also long URL segments sometimes fold into fewer tokens in ptq. buildbot: :robot_face: queued job 5409876543-token-diff: ./tools/tokenizer_diff --model rnrk-v4-int8 --slice html_url --samples 1000 cole: Could be the quant worker had a slightly different normalizer (strip_html false/true) or a different unicode normalization form in the tokenizer. Those subtle differences change token boundaries and KV alignment.\marta: Head-wise attention norms for one failure: fp16 head norms [0.18,0.14,0.32,0.10,...], int8 [0.17,0.04,0.12,0.09,...] — head 2 magnitude collapsed.\anya: Agreed. Action items I propose: 1) run per-head calibration with a stratified calibration set that includes html_url docs, 2) add a tokenizer parity check in packaging (fail on config sha mismatch), 3) add a short preproc that normalizes HTML escapes to spaced tokens as a stopgap, 4) create a golden slice of 500 html/url-heavy docs for CI top1 MRR checks.\cole: Also run hybrid eval (attention fp16) to isolate whether attention quantization is the main driver.\buildbot: queued job 5409876543-hybrid-eval: ./eval --model rnrk-v4-hybrid --slice html_url --samples 1200\marta: Quick local ablation: ptq + html-normalize recovered ~2.1% MRR, hybrid recovered ~3.0% (gap initially ~3.7%). Per-head calib run queued. anya: I'll curate the golden slice and open a PR with metadata + lightweight runner that asserts top1 MRR delta <= 1.5% vs fp16. Tagging @cole and @indra. indra: I'll take per-head calib PR and upload attention norm plots for the top 20 failures. If per-head fixes it we'll adopt for reranker PTQ recipe. buildbot: :white_check_mark: job 5409876543-token-diff completed: found 21 mismatches (mostly html escape handling and url token merges). Report: https://redwood.internal/tdiff/5409876543\cole: Thanks team. Once PRs land let's rerun full holdout. Also add a short note to onboarding checklist: \"verify HTML-escape and long-query-url slices during quantization\". anya: Will update checklist in the PR. Closing loop after rerun.
